properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): a chat recording a wrestling schedule kept 20 tournament dates as planned milestone epochs, with each date only in prose, because nothing in reflow2 carries a typed date for a scheduled real-world event, and find_tools surfaces neither plan_epoch nor any home for it
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause), 2026-10-25, on Anthony's ask from the flo2 usage baseline (hub fact:flo2-usage-baseline-2026-10-25).
① OBSERVED from flo2.io's call log (read-only; tool, outcome, type fields, and whether the arguments held a date): on 2026-10-10, Alex's Grok chat called find_tools three times ("add event calendar date dual tournament", "temporal fact dated event schedule epoch", "add artifact record document") and scan_nodes on TemporalFact. Then, between 14:48:50 and 14:49:32, it called add_artifact twice (a document) and plan_epoch 20 times with epoch_type milestone, each with a date in its arguments, all ok; one more at 14:53:25.
② PRECEDENT: dec:plan-time-axis (OPEN: should reflow2 model scheduled time as a first-class axis); fact:record-change-places-an-event-by-epoch-and-212-of-214-epochs-carry-no-date (2026-09-10); flo2's dec:idea-a-schedule-in-a-design-is-a-calendar-people-add-to-their-phone (proposed).
③-⑤ CANDIDATES, each with the measurement that could refute it:
(C1) there is nowhere to record a dated event. PARTLY REFUTED: the chat found plan_epoch, and a milestone holds an ordered point. BUT describe_schema on plan_epoch lists its fields as checksum, description, epoch_type, id, name, sequence and status. There is NO date field, and the tool takes no unknown fields. So each of the 20 dates sits only in a name or description, where nothing can sort it, flag it as past, or turn it into a calendar. SURVIVES as the main cause: no typed date for a scheduled event.
(C2) find_tools does not surface the home. MEASURED on 0.91.0: "record a schedule of dated events: tournaments, meets, calendar dates" ranks schedule_for (design items against epochs), invalidates, invalidated_findings, confirmation_ledger and record_finding, and not plan_epoch. SURVIVES as a contributor.
(C3) the fit is wrong in kind: a DesignEpoch is the DESIGN's own time (baselines, revisions, release cuts), and a tournament is an event in the world the design is about. NOT ESTABLISHED whether this misleads any read of Alex's design (his design was not read); fact:seventeen-planned-epochs-exist-and-the-loop-digest-names-none-of-them suggests loop_status raises no false "overdue". C1 and C3 cannot be told apart from the log: both predict exactly this record.
(C4, outside reflow2) the chat should have kept the schedule only in the document. It did keep the document as well (add_artifact, then documents). This is not a cause, since the person evidently wanted the dates in the design.
⑥ CLASS: reflow2 has typed time only for findings (valid_from) and the design's own change; a dated occurrence in the design's domain (a meet, a launch window, an inspection) has no field. Whether to add one is the open dec:plan-time-axis, an intent question for Anthony, not a defect in one tool. Fix options are with him.
